speaker: TICKET
text: The duke sent flowers after his men shot up my room. Three hundred blue roses. The card said he deplored the recent unpleasantness and hoped we would attend his masquerade aboard the Sovereign Sun. Tank read it twice, then held it at arm's length. Nigga deplores. Apparently. Say it again. Deplores. Nah, nigga. In his voice. I raised my chin.

speaker: TICKET
text: I deplore that my niggas missed. Tank bent over the flowers. Shawna took the card before he could wipe his eyes with it. Evidence, she said. Evidence this nigga need to hire a poet. Or better men, I said. Don't help him. Porsche counted the arrangements from the doorway. Three hundred roses. No apology to the hotel. No money for the workers who cleaned up.

speaker: TICKET
text: Nigga thinks stems are currency. Mercedes pulled a vase toward her. We can send these to the staff lounge. Tell them who paid, Shawna said. Tell them who missed, Tank said. He reached for another vase. It was heavier than expected; he lifted it easily, then discovered it blocked the entire doorway.

speaker: TICKET
text: Mercedes waited with her arms folded while he turned one way, then the other. Nigga, turn the flowers. I am turning. You turning yourself. The flowers ain't learned nothing. He finally got through sideways. Rosa, passing him in the hall, plucked one blue rose from the top. Thank you. That's from the duke. Then thank you for intercepting it. We had moved suites.

speaker: TICKET
text: Shawna wanted curtains without bullet holes and a balcony she hadn't watched men climb over. The hotel gave us the whole top floor. The manager cried while handing over the keys, and my wife quietly made him sit down and drink water before anybody asked him for anything else. Tank returned empty-handed. Can I deplore his ass off the boat tonight?

speaker: TICKET
text: Get dressed first, I said. Nigga, we got invited. The three attackers were downstairs in the custody of Commandant Odette Valeur, a forty-six-year-old woman with silver at her temples and a white uniform she wore like an argument nobody had won yet. She commanded the harbor police.

speaker: TICKET
text: She had come to arrest the men, looked at my badge, looked at the broken suite and asked who had put the fountain man in the fountain. Inez, I said. Odette nodded toward her. Good distance. Then she took the prisoners somewhere Bellario couldn't collect them with a polite note. I liked her immediately. Bellario denied everything.

speaker: TICKET
text: The duke announced that the attackers had been jealous gamblers acting without permission. Nigga, without permission from who? He left that part floating. Bellario vanished from the next day's press events, but his feather appeared on an assistant's hat, and that was almost more disrespectful. Odette visited us again the afternoon of the masquerade. Lark spread Amalia's papers across the table.

speaker: TICKET
text: Cassius put his father's bird beside them. Luc told her about the missing staff. She listened to every word. Then she looked at me. If I take this to the palace alone, it disappears into a drawer. If you show it to the whole harbor while winning his race, the drawer becomes difficult to close. Nigga, I can make it a convertible. Her mouth twitched.

speaker: TICKET
text: I've seen your driving. She gave us one useful fact: the Sovereign Sun would leave the harbor after the masquerade and reach Cinder Dock the next night. Its scheduled crew had been replaced. Some of the replacements had not volunteered. Lark stood up. Mateo? Possibly. That word is killing me. Odette held her gaze. I won't give you a better one unless I have it.

speaker: TICKET
text: Lark sat down slowly. Mercedes put an arm around her shoulders without making her look at anybody. That evening my people came down the hotel staircase like the building had spent its entire life waiting for them. Tank wore black velvet and a silver mask that covered half his face. Rosa wore a red gown and a mask made of little dark feathers.

speaker: TICKET
text: Mercedes had chosen a white suit with nothing timid about it. Porsche wore gold, from the heels to the tiny knife-shaped hairpin she insisted was purely decorative and which I respectfully chose not to investigate. Cassius wore a sling matched to his jacket. Inez had traded her ankle wrap for a high boot and carried a cane topped with a silver horse.

speaker: TICKET
text: She looked dangerous enough that several men on the staircase suddenly remembered women could tell when they were staring. Shawna came last. Black dress. Blue stones at her throat. A mask she took off before reaching me because she wanted me to see her whole face when I forgot how my lungs worked. Nigga, Tank said behind me. I know. Nigga, you see your wife?

speaker: TICKET
text: I am actively seeing her. You look like you need a chair. Go find your woman. Rosa took his hand. He found her. Shawna stopped on the step above me and straightened my collar. Try to keep the tuxedo intact. Depends how the tuxedo behaves. She kissed me. Somebody farther down the staircase started applauding. Then the whole lobby joined in.

speaker: TICKET
text: Nigga, I couldn't even kiss my wife privately in a room full of strangers anymore. Fame had become an audience with poor boundaries. I bowed anyway. The Sovereign Sun waited beyond the harbor wall, longer than a street, white and gold beneath a thousand lights. Its bow opened into a ballroom. I am telling you exactly what I saw.

speaker: TICKET
text: The front of the boat had split into two great curved doors, revealing a dance floor that seemed to float above the water. A staircase descended toward the tenders, and musicians played from balconies inside the ship's mouth. Tank stared up at it. This nigga boat got teeth? Those are columns, Rosa said. That's how they get you.

speaker: TICKET
text: A steward in a white coat led us aboard. On the wall behind him hung portraits of previous Grand Prix winners. I recognized Esteban in one, younger, standing beside Nero and Amalia with a trophy between them. Somebody had moved a large vase in front of Nero's face. Cassius stopped. I moved the vase. The steward opened his mouth. Nigga, choose your next words carefully.

speaker: TICKET
text: He shut it. We entered the ballroom together. There were dukes, actresses, drivers, singers, women who charged rich men for the pleasure of their company and rich men who believed nobody could tell. Champagne moved through the room on silver trays. A pianist played a song that made the women at our table look at one another and smile.

speaker: TICKET
text: Mercedes whispered something to Porsche, and both of them walked toward a man in a white dinner jacket before he had time to flee. That their friend? Tank asked. That look like a debt. The duke stood beneath a chandelier shaped like a crown. Aiden, he said. You honor my ship. Ship was overdue. His eyes moved over my people.

speaker: TICKET
text: Counted Cassius's sling, Inez's cane, Shawna's bare shoulders. Stopped at Odette, who had come aboard separately in a black dress with her badge at the waist. A commandant at a masquerade, he said. Odette smiled. A duke hosting one. We all enjoy costumes. Nigga, I almost proposed friendship on the spot. Aurelio turned to Shawna. I hope tonight's entertainment meets your standards.

speaker: TICKET
text: My standards are sitting beside me. She took my arm. I looked at the duke and smiled with every tooth God had trusted me with. He announced the evening's exhibition after the first dance. Two cars waited on a circular platform behind the ballroom: a silver roadster and a black coupe with a blue interior. They belonged to the prize fleet.

speaker: TICKET
text: Guests could bid for the right to challenge the leading driver in a short timed run along the ship's upper deck. Nigga had put a racetrack on a yacht. I finally understood why rich people kept getting invited places. Sometimes one of them had a good idea. The duke held up a little gold key. The challenger wagers fifty thousand.

speaker: TICKET
text: If he defeats Captain Aiden, he keeps the roadster. If he loses? I asked. The money supports the Grand Prix. The workers? The institution. Nigga, the institution can get a job. My races pay the workers. A murmur crossed the room. Aurelio watched the faces around him and adjusted smoothly. Of course. Tonight's proceeds shall go to the staff.

speaker: TICKET
text: Porsche, across the room, raised her phone so he could see it recording. Say the amount too. He said it. Then Inez stepped forward. I'll race. Cassius caught her elbow. Your ankle. It's my left ankle. And still attached to the rest of you. She looked at him. He looked back. Something quiet happened between them. Not soft exactly.

speaker: TICKET
text: Two people recognizing the same fear from opposite sides. She lowered her hand. Fine. I'll choose his challenger. The duke laughed. And whom do you choose? She pointed at him. The whole ballroom turned. Aurelio's smile remained. Only his eyes moved. I do not usually— Nigga, you own the competition, I reminded him. Drive something. The applause began at our table. Spread outward.

speaker: TICKET
text: Became impossible to ignore without looking smaller than the portrait behind him. He handed his glass to Bellario's assistant. All right, he said. The duke's assistant tried to hand me a waiver. "Nigga, what's this?" "Acknowledgment of the exhibition." "I acknowledge that nigga challenged the room and the room pointed at him." Inez took the paper.

speaker: TICKET
text: "It says he's not responsible for disappointment." "Which nigga?" Tank asked. "The duke." "That nigga responsible for half mine already." Aurelio held out his hand for the page. "Shall we drive?" "Nigga," I said, "I've been dressed for it since the harbor." Shawna kissed my cheek. "Go. The nigga's gloves are getting nervous." We went up to the deck.

speaker: TICKET
text: The track circled the yacht's upper level around two pools, a glass conservatory and a helipad. The cars had been arranged for display, but the road was real enough and wide enough to make a bad decision feel generous. Floodlights shone over the water. Guests lined the balconies below us.

speaker: TICKET
text: The captain's bridge glowed at the front of the ship, guarded by two men in dark coats. I watched those men while the duke chose the silver roadster. Lark had gone below with Luc to look for familiar crew. Mercedes and Porsche followed a steward who had whispered to them at the bar. Shawna stayed at the railing with Rosa and Odette.

speaker: TICKET
text: Nobody needed to be taken away from me to have something to do. My people were already moving. Aurelio pulled on leather gloves. Do you know what the difference is between a guest and an owner? he asked. Guest can leave without selling the furniture. An owner decides when the evening ends. Nigga, we'll see. We started together. He was good.

speaker: TICKET
text: That surprised me for half a second. Then it pleased me. I wanted the man to have at least one real thing to lose. His roadster took the first curve cleanly. I stayed close in the black coupe. We swept around the glass conservatory with the sea falling away beyond the rail.

speaker: TICKET
text: He accelerated toward the helipad, then moved across my line hard enough to make his intention plain. This wasn't a polite exhibition. Good. I came around the outside. He tried to shut the gap. I let him think he had, then took the next turn so close to the pool that water rose over my left wheels. The guests below screamed.

speaker: TICKET
text: On the far balcony, Tank was jumping up and down in his velvet suit like a furious wedding cake. Nigga, get him! I got him. At the final bend I moved alongside the duke, looked straight across into his car and smiled. He saw it. Lost one fraction of a second deciding whether to hate me or the smile. I used the fraction.

speaker: TICKET
text: The black coupe crossed the line first. I stopped at the railing. The ballroom below erupted. Aurelio rolled to a halt beside me, both hands still on the wheel. For the first time all night he looked his age. I got out and held up the car's key. For the staff, I said. The cheering doubled. Then a gunshot came from below deck.

speaker: TICKET
text: The cheering stopped so abruptly I could hear the ocean against the hull. Shawna was already moving toward the stairway. I jumped the low rail, landed on the lower platform and reached her at the door. Rosa and Odette were behind her. Tank thundered down from the other side.

speaker: TICKET
text: Lark came out of a corridor carrying a man whose white shirt was stained at the shoulder. Luc held his other arm. Mercedes followed with three women in crew uniforms. Porsche came last, face hard, a broken champagne bottle in her hand. Somebody asked the wrong question, she said. Behind them, two guards rounded the corner. Odette showed her badge. Stop. One lifted his gun.

speaker: TICKET
text: I hit him with the door. Nigga, it was a beautiful door. Heavy wood, brass edge. Somebody had paid excellent money for it to become part of his problem. His weapon struck the floor. Tank caught the second man against the corridor wall and made the wall reconsider its career. Shawna took the wounded crewman's weight from Lark. Where's Mateo? Lark asked him.

speaker: TICKET
text: The man shook his head, breath catching. Island. They moved him ahead. She went pale. Alive? He nodded. Yes. For a second she couldn't stand. Mercedes caught her around the waist. Nigga alive, she said firmly. Hear that part first. The wounded man looked at Cassius, who had reached us with Inez. Chrome? Cassius froze. Yes. The man's eyes filled. Your father said you'd come.

speaker: TICKET
text: Cassius made a sound I had never heard from him, not when his car hung over the cliff, not when we read the letter. It was smaller than a word and much harder to hear. Aurelio appeared at the top of the stairs. Captain, this has become disorderly. I turned toward him. Nigga, I haven't started. Below us, the yacht's great bow doors began closing.

speaker: TICKET
text: The ballroom narrowed around the sea. He was ending the evening. I looked at the black coupe above us, then at the open front of the ship, then at the harbor launch approaching beyond it with blue lights flashing. Odette followed my eyes. No, she said. Yes, I said. You cannot drive a car through the ballroom. Nigga, watch the piano. Tank started laughing.

speaker: TICKET
text: That was all the encouragement a man like me required.
